content.value_statement: Data brokerage teams need structured methods to match parties, verify eligibility, and protect fees. This skill provides workflows, checklists, and document outlines for each stage.
actual_capabilities: Compares matching, agency, and sponsorship brokerage models by responsibilities, fees, and risk.
Structures seller resource pools and buyer requirement lists.
Creates bilateral verification checklists covering ownership, quality, compliance, eligibility, payment capacity, and intended use.
Drafts transaction plans, intermediary agreement outlines, sponsorship letter outlines, and commission records.
Applies a ten-stage workflow from brokerage positioning through ecosystem maintenance.
Reviews engagements against qualification, documentation, delivery, commission, and role-boundary controls.
limitations: It cannot independently verify ownership, identity, payment capacity, data quality, or regulatory status.
It does not replace legal counsel, regulators, licensed exchanges, or qualified sponsorship institutions.
Its policy references and fee ranges require confirmation for the relevant date and jurisdiction.
Generated agreements and sponsorship materials are drafts and require authorized professional review.

use_cases.title: Select a Brokerage Model
use_cases.description: Compare matching, agency, and sponsorship roles, then define responsibilities, services, fees, and required qualifications.

use_cases.title: Verify a Proposed Transaction
use_cases.description: Build separate evidence checklists for the seller, buyer, data product, intended use, and payment readiness.

use_cases.title: Protect Brokerage Revenue
use_cases.description: Outline commission terms, participation records, anti-circumvention clauses, delivery checkpoints, and settlement controls.

prompt_templates.title: Choose My Brokerage Role
prompt_templates.prompt: We serve [industry] clients in [region]. Compare matching, agency, and sponsorship models for us. Recommend one role with responsibilities, qualifications, fees, and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Verification Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a bilateral verification checklist for this transaction: [details]. Separate seller evidence, buyer evidence, data quality, ownership, compliance, intended use, and payment checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Brokerage Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a brokerage plan for [transaction]. Include matching logic, responsibilities, milestones, negotiation points, delivery controls, commission terms, anti-circumvention protections, and unresolved risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Full Operating Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our brokerage process and documents: [materials]. Map gaps against the ten-stage workflow, prioritize risks, assign owners, and propose measurable acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Compare brokerage roles for a small firm that has buyer relationships but no sponsorship qualification.
output: Scope: identify needs, match suppliers, coordinate validation, and support contracting.
Boundary: do not issue sponsorship opinions or guarantee compliance.
Revenue: documented commission or fixed service fee, subject to local market validation.

output_examples.input: Create buyer-side checks for a healthcare data transaction.
output: Confirm legal identity, authority, payment capacity, and procurement approval.
Document the intended purpose, access population, retention period, security controls, and deletion method.
Escalate healthcare, privacy, cross-border, and secondary-use questions to qualified reviewers.
Stop the transaction when purpose or authorization evidence remains incomplete.

output_examples.input: Review a commission arrangement that has no written anti-circumvention term.
output_examples.output: High-priority gap: the broker has limited evidence protecting its fee. Add written scope, introduced parties, commission triggers, survival period, records, settlement timing, and dispute terms.

best_practices: Confirm current laws, exchange rules, qualifications, and fee assumptions before using any recommendation.
Keep dated evidence for seller claims, buyer eligibility, intended use, negotiations, delivery, acceptance, and commission triggers.
Separate advisory drafts from official opinions and obtain authorized legal, compliance, and sponsorship approval.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a supplier statement as proof of ownership, quality, legality, or authorization.
Do not issue guarantees, legal conclusions, or sponsorship opinions without authority and documented review.
Do not begin delivery while buyer purpose, contract terms, security controls, or payment conditions remain unclear.

faq.question: Does this skill provide or sell data?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning guidance and document outlines for connecting buyers, sellers, and professional service providers.

faq.question: Can it verify that a data product is lawful?
faq.answer: No. It can organize evidence requests, but qualified reviewers must verify ownership, privacy, security, and sector requirements.

faq.question: Can it produce a final intermediary agreement?
faq.answer: It can draft an outline and issue checklist. Licensed counsel should adapt and approve the final agreement.

faq.question: Can it issue a sponsorship letter?
faq.answer: It can prepare a draft outline. Only an authorized institution should conduct the review, accept responsibility, and issue the final letter.

faq.question: Are the listed commission ranges authoritative?
faq.answer: No. They are reference ranges from the knowledge base and require current market, contract, tax, and jurisdiction review.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the parties, data product, intended use, jurisdiction, transaction stage, available evidence, commercial terms, and known constraints.
